note: A primitive camping loop of its own beside the Highway 169 bridge over the Platte River: an oval gravel lane about 75 m long under big scattered hardwoods, sites around and inside it, a privy at its entrance. The river is 45-60 m east of the loop behind a band of bottomland timber and a sandbar. The fishing-access lot is 200 m further on, where the gravel drive ends at the bank. --Claude
summary: Confirmed, and not a lot: MDC 'Individual Campsites' ('This area offers camping and access to the Platte River') at a separate gravel camping loop with a privy; the river-access lot is 200 m north. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; privy written; phone matches; pin is inside the loop. Stored riverview is not supported by anything I can show: the loop is 45-60 m from the river behind about 45 m of timber - flagged as a lead down.
flags: INCLUSION (stays - a built camping loop, the lot rule does not arise): area page 'This area offers camping and access to the Platte River', 'Camping: Individual Campsites'. No brochure. The map (10/08) draws a loop road off the entrance drive with the Primitive Camping Area symbol inside it and a Privy, a Parking Lot square and the Disabled Accessible symbol at its entrance; a second Parking Lot is at the end of the drive on the river bank 200 m north. GIS layer 27: one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (OBJECTID 143) at 39.90837,-94.69159 = the stored pin, inside the loop; lots 1352 (39 m, at the loop entrance) and 1351 (195 m, the river lot). On the 0.21 m/px leaf-off frame the loop is an oval gravel lane about 75 x 45 m with large scattered trees, a small building (privy) at its west entrance, and three vehicles parked on the grass inside and beside the lane. Site count is unpublished and not countable from the frame.

WATERFRONT LEAD DOWN (stored riverview, evidence 'camping loop in the grove beside the river behind a tree band'): measured on the 190 m frame, from the loop's east edge it is about 46 m to the edge of the sandbar and about 59 m to the water; from the GIS point in the middle of the loop about 75 m to the sandbar. Between is a continuous band of bottomland hardwoods about 45 m deep (open understorey, bare in this frame), no road and no day use. The Platte is about 35-45 m wide here. The access lot at the north end is on the bank, but that is the day-use lot, not the camp. There are no official campsite photos. Leaf-off the sandbar and water probably show through the trunks from the east side of the loop; in leaf I cannot say. Nothing is within 50 m on open ground. Rippee (65-80 m behind 40-60 m of timber) was held at not waterfront last batch; by the unsure-goes-down rule this one goes to not waterfront unless a leaf-off glimpse through 45 m of timber is accepted as riverview.

ACCESS: 'From St. Joseph, take Highway 169 north 10 miles to area entrance.' The gravel drive leaves paved Highway 169 at the west end of the river bridge; about 250 m to the loop. No ford or limit. The loop is in the river bottom and would flood with the Platte; no closure is posted now.
PIN: stored 39.90837,-94.69159 is the GIS point inside the loop. No move.
PHONE: stored 816-271-3100 matches the area page's 'For more information call (816) 271-3100'.
SEASON: stored year_round (manual) stands; nothing dates the camping.
